title: Which move changed the position?
outcomes: Spots the opponent move that touches something the old plan needs
Keeps the plan when the opponent's move changed nothing it needs
Re-picks the plan after a change instead of continuing the old one

steps.text: In *A new valuation after every change* you restated the plan after a stated change. Here nobody tells you what changed. Look at the opponent's last move and ask: **does it touch a square, a piece or a pawn that my plan needs?** If it does, re-pick the plan. If it does not, keep it. Switching plans every move is as bad as never switching.

A move can change the evaluation in two ways: it creates something to capture or attack (a piece left loose, a new pawn), or it removes a square your plan needs. A quiet king move or a rook shuffle usually does neither. As a *rule of thumb*, name the changed fact in one sentence before you switch.

steps.title: Did the plan survive?
steps.prompt: Board 1: White planned Ne2 and Black played ...Kh8. Is Ne2 still good? Board 2: Black played ...e5 instead. Is Ne2 still good? Board 3: Black played the quiet ...Qd7 in a similar position. Is there anything to re-pick? Predict each, then check.
For each silent position, what was the plan and what was the opponent's last move? Did you change the plan, and what fact had changed?

sources: items: IBds57-20..25 and IBds57-34 (authored sequences made by playing one opponent move in a position; the plan moves are named in the prompts and are not claims about any game)
